stem:
Priya's grandmother follows a purely lunar calendar in which each month begins with a new Moon. Priya notices that over the years the same lunar month falls in different seasons.

Why does a purely lunar calendar not keep the same months aligned with the same seasons?

options.text: The Moon's phases change more slowly each year
The seasons are caused by clouds and rainfall
Twelve lunar months are about 354 days, shorter than the 365-day seasonal year
The Moon's light is brighter in some seasons

teacher.key_rationale: Twelve lunar months total about 354 days, which is roughly 11 days shorter than the ~365-day seasonal (solar) year, so lunar months drift earlier each year relative to the seasons. Options A, B, D are incorrect statements about the cause of seasons or lunar phases.
